summary: @servicetitan/carto-charts-core preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated in-tarball payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-array indirection) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (or uses a local bun on PATH), extracts the platform-specific bun binary, chmod +x it, and execFileSyncs it against a sibling file math_init.js in the package root. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated payload (numeric+string constant array plus a WV8StW string-array shuffling function; sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc). Both setup.mjs and math_init.js sit at the tarball root but are outside the author-declared files allowlist in package.json ("files":["dist","README.md"]), indicating they were smuggled into the published tarball outside the normal build. The package advertises itself as an ECharts theme/data-viz layer with no DOM and no rendering — there is no legitimate reason for such a library to fetch a second runtime at install time to execute an opaque obfuscated blob. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: Bun is fetched specifically to run an in-tarball payload that scanners inspecting Node-resolved code would not analyze. Installing the package causes attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's host at npm install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
